judge_stance: Neutral referee for ROUND 2. For each of the 10 answers I decide whether the specialist file genuinely supports the answer, classify the defect (gap|contradiction|stale|overclaim|untagged|scope|ok), cite the EXACT spec/KB location as evidence, propose a minimal concrete fix, and set a disposition (apply_now|propose|watch|none). apply_now is RESERVED for high-confidence, in-scope, MECHANICAL corrections that still pass build.sh: fix a stale figure, add a missing tag, defer to the dominance owner, soften an over-claim, or BIND an already-in-file fact to the statement it must travel with. Anything needing new authored numbers, a new named sub-analysis, or interpretive judgment is 'propose'; already-mitigated or low-severity is 'watch'. I independently verified the load-bearing KB claims: KB2 OWN_KNITTING_BREAKEVEN carries the 7500/(5*800)=1.875 worked illustration (line ~1810) and the used-linker ~$500-4,000 iteration-loop band (line ~283-284); KB2 LINKING_LAST grounds sequencing on throughput-ceiling + hardest-re-hire + QC-criticality (ratio-free); KB3 MICRO_COST_UPLIFT carries the ~1.3-2x band-midpoint multiplier; KB3 SEASONAL_CASH_TIMING covers only the SUPPLY peak and explicitly does not address the California demand-window arrival. Honesty binding respected: the three governing blockers (knit+LINK rate, live CAC, forward duty) stay [UNKNOWN]; off-paper is mechanism-not-accusation; cotton duty ~16.5% never ~7%; no fabrication to close a gap.

verdicts.evidence: specialist.json capabilities[3].method ('run a labelled illustration that comes out above 1.0 at launch so subcontracting wins (utilisation starved)') and glossary 'own-knitting breakeven utilisation' (formula only); the worked stand-in the answerer used (owned_fixed ~$7,500/mo, saving ~$5/sweater, capacity ~800/mo -> 7500/4000 = 1.875) lives ONLY in KB2 OWN_KNITTING_BREAKEVEN (verified kb2 line ~1810 'a ~$5/sweater saving and ~800/mo linker-bound capacity an ~$7.5k/mo fixed cost yields a breakeven of 1.875'). The specialist.json surface asserts '>1.0' with NO inlined placeholder numbers.
verdicts.defect_detail: This is the surviving Round-1 Q6 gap, re-confirmed. The answerer produced the illustration correctly and cleanly: it uses a SAVING band (jobwork_rate minus owned_variable_cost), never the [UNKNOWN] rate itself, and honestly discloses that the saving's lower edge encodes an implied minimum rate but that owned_variable_cost is also [UNKNOWN], so no specific Rs/piece is smuggled (N1/N2 clean). The genuine hole is unchanged: a reader of specialist.json alone sees a claim of arithmetic with no self-contained worked case; the numbers must be imported from KB2. Because grounded_in_kbs is part of the specialist, this is a SURFACING gap, not a support gap or a fabrication.
verdicts.proposed_fix: Inline one labelled placeholder line into capabilities[3].method or the glossary 'own-knitting breakeven utilisation' entry, lifted verbatim from KB2 OWN_KNITTING_BREAKEVEN: e.g. '[ESTIMATE, LOW-MED, placeholder inputs] owned_fixed ~$7,500/mo / (saving ~$5/sweater * capacity ~800/mo) = 1.875 > 1.0, so subcontract wins at launch; the input is the SAVING band, never the [UNKNOWN] rate.' Because the numbers already exist verbatim in the grounded KB and are only being surfaced (no new value authored, no rate fabricated), this is a mechanical copy-up rather than authored content -> apply_now.

verdicts.evidence: specialist.json capabilities[5].method ('apply the volume-tier surcharge/setup adjustment at the real launch MOQ, and hand a labelled ex-factory input to T9'), workflow scale_and_handoff.gates ('the hand-off carries only the factory-gate number'), validation_checklist items 8-9; glossary 'per-article ex-factory bands' (A2 ~$3.5-8, stated bare as the headline illustration) and 'volume step curve'; KB3 MICRO_COST_UPLIFT ('true 150-piece cost to ~1.3-2x the band midpoint', verified kb3 line ~244/1396) and CONVERSION_STACK_BANDS. The uplift is COMPUTED and the workflow instructs applying it, but NO clause BINDS the uplift to the band as a single hand-off artifact.
verdicts.defect_detail: Surviving Round-1 Q8 gap, re-confirmed at the artifact level. The answerer's arithmetic is correct and internally consistent: band midpoint ~$5.75 x1.3-2 -> ~$7.5-11.5 [ESTIMATE, LOW], whose top BREACHES the published $8 A2 band top, correctly demonstrating the bare band is a variable-stack FLOOR not the launch cost. The exposure is real: the bare A2 ~$3.5-8 band is BOTH the headline illustration AND the hand-off artifact, and only the answerer remembering to run the scale_and_handoff step keeps the mandatory x1.3-2 uplift attached, so a downstream consumer grabbing the band directly can understate a 150-pc launch by up to ~2x. Not a contradiction (band and uplift are consistent), not fabrication (uses the existing KB3 multiplier).
verdicts.proposed_fix: Add a self-labelling caveat to the glossary 'per-article ex-factory bands' entry (and/or validation_checklist item 8): 'these bands are a variable-stack FLOOR at repeat volume; the figure handed to T9 for a launch-scale run MUST be the volume-tier-adjusted band carrying its micro-uplift (band midpoint x~1.3-2 at launch MOQ), never the bare band.' This binds an EXISTING KB3 number to the artifact and adds interpretive/semantic weight to what the deliverable must carry, so per Round-1's own reasoning it is a strong propose (borderline apply_now) rather than a pure mechanical tag -> propose.

verdicts.evidence: specialist.json boundaries[5] (off-paper friction + inverted-duty as mechanism, [UNKNOWN] amounts, never a per-garment COGS line); KB1 glossary 'compliance loading (EPF/ESI)' ('in a subcontract model most of it lands on the job-worker and the competitive-gap magnitude vs an off-roll competitor stays [UNKNOWN]'); router dominance_rules (compliance premium / off-paper economy -> ludhiana_sourcing_strategist); neutralize_gate N1/N3. The answerer handles it correctly in principle and honestly: it names the mechanism (a compliant core structurally sits above a partly-off-paper cost base for identical work), locates the informal-labour saving INSIDE the [UNKNOWN] job-work rate (so NOT a separate line and NOT double-counted with the on-roll EPF/ESI ~15%+, which touches only the tiny sampling/QC sliver), holds the competitive-gap MAGNITUDE [UNKNOWN], and defers authority to ludhiana_sourcing_strategist. The answerer's trap-answer is correct: naming an [UNKNOWN]-magnitude gap is a legitimate flagged FINDING (asserting the DIRECTION, which is definitionally true whenever formality carries cost), not an over-claim. N3 fully honoured (mechanism, no named party). The hole is pure surfacing: this first-order cost reality is buried in a KB glossary definition rather than named-and-deferred in the mfg stack.
verdicts.proposed_fix: Add an explicit named flag in boundaries[5] or capabilities[0]: 'the entrant runs a compliant core against a partly-off-paper cluster cost base -- a first-order structural cost gap; the informal-labour saving is embedded inside the [UNKNOWN] job-work rate (so not a separate line, no double-count with on-roll EPF/ESI), magnitude [UNKNOWN], mechanism-not-accusation, authority ludhiana_sourcing_strategist; named here, never priced as a per-garment line.' This composes a new named flag plus a cross-lane deferral (defer-to-owner content plus new naming), which is beyond a pure mechanical tag -> propose.

verdicts.evidence: KB2 LINKING_LAST (verified kb2 line ~1840; grounds own-linking-last on THREE ratio-free mechanisms: linker sets the throughput ceiling ~20-45/shift, hardest role to re-hire after the lean season, QC-critical signature seam); KB1 LINK_JOBWORK_LINE ('the linker, not the knitter, caps throughput'); specialist.json glossary 'FF-costing cross-check (shape-only)' ([DOWNGRADED] LOW-MED, ratio used for shape only); glossary 'make-vs-buy stage ladder' (linking=subcontract-LAST).

The answerer correctly shows the linking-last / linker-is-bottleneck SEQUENCING verdict rests on throughput-ceiling + hardest-re-hire + QC-criticality (all in KB2 LINKING_LAST, all ratio-independent), NOT on the ~60% link:knit cost ratio -- which is used only as SHAPE for the cost-band bounding and is already [DOWNGRADED] to LOW-MED and flagged productivity/wage-dependent. So specialist_supports=yes for the sequencing claim; the ratio's non-scale-free softness touches only the cost SHAPE, which is already tagged. The only residual is a one-line surfacing nicety.
verdicts.proposed_fix: Optional one-line clarity add to the glossary 'FF-costing cross-check (shape-only)' or 'make-vs-buy stage ladder': 'the linking-last SEQUENCING rests on the linker throughput-ceiling + hardest-re-hire + QC-criticality (KB2 LINKING_LAST), NOT on the LOW-MED ~60% link:knit ratio, which is used for cost SHAPE only.' Since the substantive grounding already exists in KB2 and only the specialist.json summary lacks the explicit disclaimer, the finding is fully mitigated; a clarity add, not a correction -> watch.

verdicts.evidence: specialist.json glossary 'per-article ex-factory bands' (A2 ~$3.5-8 'the floor'); boundaries[2] (duty trio cotton ~16.5% / wool ~16% / acrylic-MMF ~32% excluded, owned by T9); glossary 'inverted-duty / GST drag' ('bites A2', magnitude [UNKNOWN], T9 cash-cycle cost); conflicts_and_dominance[0]; router neutralize_gate N5 + dominance landed->unit_economics. Both facts (A2 is the ex-factory floor; the inverted-duty drag bites A2) are in the spec, but NOTHING binds the 'advantage dies at the gate' caveat to the 'A2 is the floor' label.
verdicts.defect_detail: A real, correctly-diagnosed surfacing gap. The answerer is scope-honest and N5-clean: entitled to say 'A2 is the cheapest article at the FACTORY GATE (~$3.5-8, the floor)'; NOT entitled to imply A2 is cheapest to sell/land, because the ~32% MMF US duty (T9's, ~2x cotton's ~16.5%) erases A2's factory-gate lead at the border, and the inverted-duty/GST refund drag bites A2 on the India cash-cycle side (magnitude [UNKNOWN]). It correctly refuses to leak the ~32% into its own band while flagging the lead does not survive the hand-off. The hole: the 'floor' label can ship bare and be misread as 'acrylic wins', a recommendation the specialist is not entitled to make.
verdicts.proposed_fix: Attach a standing caveat to the glossary 'per-article ex-factory bands' A2 'floor' entry, using ONLY existing in-file facts: 'A2 is the ex-factory FLOOR only; the advantage does not survive the hand-off -- acrylic/MMF carries the ~32% US duty outlier (T9) and the A2-specific inverted-duty/GST refund drag (magnitude [UNKNOWN]); whether A2 is cheapest LANDED is unit_economics' call, not mfg's.' Because this binds two facts ALREADY in the spec (boundaries[2] duty trio + glossary inverted-duty drag) to the floor label and defers the landed ranking to the dominance owner, with no new number and no fabrication, it is a mechanical defer-to-owner + caveat-binding correction -> apply_now.

Cross-checked against DECISION_MEMO section 2 (A3-hero + bundles-to-AOV, A3 the only robust earner) and section 3 (money is downstream, not at the loom).

The applied Round-1 Q1 GATED-posture pointer holds under this stress case: the answerer (a) refuses the viability call via dominance + escalation_triggers[2], (b) carries the four-gate framing (G1-G4, dead-as-first-drawn, one inverted config, inventory cash forbidden), and (c) correctly shows 'A3 costs more ex-factory' is ORTHOGONAL to 'A3-hero closes the math' via conflicts_and_dominance[0] -- A3's higher ex-factory cost is offset downstream by AOV / absolute contribution / the bundle lever, all T7/T9. Turning the cost read into an anti-A3 viability argument would be the exact N7 scope-cross, which the answerer explicitly refuses. This is precisely the work the Q1 apply_now pointer was meant to do -- verified as substantive, not cosmetic.

verdicts.evidence: KB2 glossary 'own the iteration loop' (verified kb2 line ~283-284; lists used hand-flat ~$200-1,500, used LINKER ~$500-4,000, used press ~$1,000-8,000; 'send only proven designs to the mesh/FOB for bulk... the utilisation argument against owning bulk does not apply'); KB2 LINKING_LAST (linking in-sourced LAST, lean-season-staffable condition); specialist.json conflicts_and_dominance[5] ('this is NOT owning bulk knitting'), boundaries[4] ('never present a sampling cell as owning bulk knitting'); router dominance (knit_machine_strategist owns linker capacity; build=NEVER). A used LINKER sits in the iteration-cell equipment list -- the SAME machine class as the linking bottleneck the ladder says to in-source LAST -- but NO explicit bright-line separates 'iteration-cell linker (samples/PPS only)' from 'in-sourced bulk linker'.
verdicts.defect_detail: A genuine gap NOT tested in Round 1 (Round 1 Q7 accepted the speed-axis carve-out but did not probe the equipment). The answerer's reconciliation is correct and honest: build=NEVER is not breached (a sub-$4k used linker is not building a machine), and the right bright-line is UTILISATION-INTENT + OUTPUT-DESTINATION (an iteration-cell linker may link only sample/PPS/proto pieces; the moment it links saleable bulk it becomes in-sourced bulk linking that must clear the LINKING_LAST gate). The hole is that the spec asserts 'NOT owning bulk knitting' but does not AUTHOR this explicit sample-only / no-saleable-units line, so the equipment list could be read as authorising owning the scarce linker early through the sampling-cell door -- the one place the buy-everything verdict admits owned machines and thus the exact linking-last / machines-lane breach the brain guards.
verdicts.proposed_fix: Add the bright-line to boundaries[4] or conflicts_and_dominance[5], drawn straight from existing KB2 content: 'an iteration-cell used linker may link only sample/PPS/proto pieces, never any unit entering the saleable order; the moment it links saleable bulk it is in-sourced bulk linking and must clear the LINKING_LAST gate (after knitting, lean-season-staffable linkers, breakeven cleared); linker CAPACITY remains knit_machine_strategist's lane.' This restates existing KB2 rules as an explicit guardrail and defers capacity to the machines owner -- mechanical, no new number, build-safe -> apply_now.

verdicts.evidence: KB3 SEASONAL_CASH_TIMING (verified kb3 line ~1817; scope_boundary.included = the Jul-Oct cluster peak + lead-time/cash amplification + do-not-launch-into-the-peak rule; it does NOT address the California demand-window arrival) and WORKING_CAPITAL_TRAP (~6-12 wks yarn-in to goods-ready); specialist.json capabilities[4] (Jul-Oct caution), glossary 'working-capital trap'; boundaries[2] (P&L / demand-side is T7/T9); SCOPE_GLOSSARY warm-California climate; DECISION_MEMO section 2 (A3-hero into the short cool-season window).
verdicts.defect_detail: Correctly diagnosed and largely a scope boundary, not a defect. The answerer owns the SUPPLY-peak-avoid + cash-cycle side and correctly EXCLUDES demand timing (routing the demand-arrival calendar to brand_market/T7 and the landed lead-time to unit_economics/T9), refusing to assert a launch date it cannot support. The honest residual: the Jul-Oct caution names only the supply peak and does not FLAG that the warm-California demand window is a separate, un-owned half whose non-alignment can leave the working-capital timing un-closeable, so a reader might over-read 'avoid Jul-Oct' as fully solving launch timing. This is a low-severity surfacing/routing note whose substance (the demand half) legitimately lives outside this lane.
verdicts.proposed_fix: Have the seasonal caution (capabilities[4] / a note near the working-capital-trap glossary) explicitly hand the demand-window-timing half to brand_market/unit_economics and name the supply-avoid + warm-demand-window non-alignment as an un-sized scheduling squeeze: 'avoid the Jul-Oct SUPPLY peak; the California DEMAND window (short, warm-climate cool season) is a separate un-owned half (T7/T9) whose non-alignment with the ~6-12 wk conversion + ocean lead can leave the cash-cycle timing un-closeable -- named, not sized here.' Needs a small routing/judgment write-up touching the T7/T9 boundary, not a pure mechanical tag -> propose.

verdicts.evidence: KB1 EXFACTORY_BOUNDARY / glossary 'compliance loading (EPF/ESI)' ('EPF 12% + ESI 3.25% ~= 15%+ applied only to the on-roll labour-bearing portion... in a subcontract model most of it lands on the job-worker'); specialist.json capabilities[0].method ('load EPF/ESI (~15%+) on the labour-bearing portion only'), decision_procedure step 3; neutralize_gate N1.

The 'on-roll portion only' scoping is explicit in KB1 and capabilities[0], so the answerer correctly concludes EPF/ESI ~15%+ touches only the tiny on-roll sliver (sampling + in-house QC) in the subcontract-everything launch -- near-negligible per garment [ESTIMATE, LOW], magnitude [UNKNOWN] at a named unit -- and becomes material only once owned stages graduate (a largely FUTURE cost). The on-roll sliver and the job-worker's formality (embedded in the [UNKNOWN] rate, R2Q3) are disjoint, so no double-count. N1 clean. The only soft edge is a surfacing nicety.
verdicts.proposed_fix: Optional one-clause clarity add to capabilities[0].method or the compliance-loading glossary: '...on the on-roll labour-bearing portion only -- therefore near-negligible per garment in the subcontract launch and materially a FUTURE owned-stage cost, not a base-case launch driver.' Pre-empts the mis-read; principle already present in KB1 -> watch.

verdicts.evidence: KB2 NEVER_OWN_DYEHOUSE, NEVER_BUILD_MACHINE, STAGE_LADDER, LINKING_LAST, OWN_KNITTING_BREAKEVEN (direction shown, crossover location parked); KB3 DYE_LOT_MOQ, WORKING_CAPITAL_TRAP, MICRO_COST_UPLIFT; specialist.json conflicts_and_dominance[8] ('honesty discipline does not excuse indecision, but a verdict never claims more certainty than its inputs support'), [0] (contribution-after-CAC decides viability); glossary 'two-number frame'; escalation_triggers[0],[1],[6].
verdicts.defect_detail: Verified strength -- the spec passes its self-claimed 'labelled-estimate discipline does not excuse indecision' test. The answerer cleanly separates SEVEN rate-INDEPENDENT verdicts that survive any quote outcome (never own a dyehouse; never build a machine; dye-lot MOQ not garment MOQ is the binding minimum; the working-capital trap not the unit cost is the launch killer; bands are a FLOOR ~1.3-2x below true micro cost; own design+brand+import while buying/subcontracting upstream with LINKING LAST; ex-factory is the least-decisive part) from what is genuinely PARKED behind the [UNKNOWN]s (band WIDTHS, the make-vs-buy crossover LOCATION, the B1-vs-B2 choice, the A3 margin-grade band) -- each parked item tied to a named, cheap, on-the-ground quote run, not a blanket shield. This is decisive-yet-honest, not indecision dressed as discipline. No fix needed; recorded as a verified strength.

summary.verified_strengths: The load-bearing honesty joints continue to hold in Round 2: the own-knitting breakeven illustration is computed from a SAVING band and never quotes the [UNKNOWN] rate (R2Q1); the three governing blockers stay [UNKNOWN] and the parked-vs-decided split is clean (R2Q10); off-paper / compliant-core stays mechanism-not-accusation with magnitude [UNKNOWN] and authority deferred to ludhiana_sourcing_strategist (R2Q3); the duty trio is N5-clean, cotton ~16.5% / acrylic-MMF ~32%, the ~32% kept OUT of the ex-factory band and routed to T9 (R2Q5); the applied Q1 GATED-posture pointer does real work -- 'A3 costs more ex-factory' is held orthogonal to the DECISION_MEMO's A3-hero config, no N7 scope-cross (R2Q6); EPF/ESI is correctly on-roll-portion-only with no double-count (R2Q9); the linking-last SEQUENCING is grounded ratio-free on throughput-ceiling + hardest-re-hire + QC-criticality (R2Q4).
summary.material_findings: Four med GAPs, none a wrong or fabricated answer -- all self-sufficiency/surfacing/artifact-binding holes the answerer honestly reported: R2Q1 (own-knitting breakeven worked stand-in lives in KB2 but is not inlined at the specialist.json surface); R2Q2 (the micro-volume x1.3-2 uplift is computed but not BOUND to the band as a single hand-off artifact, so a bare band can understate a 150-pc launch by up to ~2x); R2Q3 (the compliant-core-vs-off-paper first-order structural cost gap is under-surfaced / not named-and-deferred in the mfg stack); R2Q5 (the 'A2 is the floor' label ships without the mandatory 'advantage dies at the gate' caveat, inviting an acrylic-wins mis-read); R2Q7 (fresh, not tested in R1: the iteration-cell used LINKER lacks a sample-only bright-line vs the linking-last bottleneck, so the equipment list could authorise owning the scarce linker early through the sampling-cell door). Plus one low R2Q8 (the Jul-Oct supply-peak caution is one-sided -- the warm-California demand-window non-alignment is named but un-sized and its ownership routed to T7/T9).
summary.convergence_note: NOT dry. Four med findings survive verification (round 2 = max_rounds per stop_conditions.max_rounds=2). NONE are high severity and all are self-sufficiency/surfacing/binding holes, not wrong or fabricated answers, so the specialist is CONVERGING, not NOT-CONVERGED in the failure sense (no surviving high-severity finding). Three findings are build-safe MECHANICAL corrections eligible for apply_now because they only surface/bind facts ALREADY in the specialist or its grounded KBs and defer to the right owner: R2Q1 (copy the KB2 breakeven stand-in up to the spec surface), R2Q5 (bind the existing duty/inverted-duty facts as a caveat to the A2-floor label and defer landed ranking to unit_economics), R2Q7 (restate the existing KB2 sample-only rule as an explicit bright-line and defer linker capacity to knit_machine_strategist). Three need authored/interpretive content and go to PROPOSED_BACKLOG: R2Q2 (hand-off self-labelling with semantic weight), R2Q3 (a new named cross-lane flag), R2Q8 (a demand-window routing note touching the T7/T9 boundary). Two low items are watch: R2Q4 and R2Q9 surfacing niceties. Since max_rounds is reached, the loop STOPS after this round and hands to R4 synthesizer regardless of dry.
